headline: Speaking more languages may keep the brain younger

sources.title: Speaking multiple languages may slow brain aging by years, study finds
Multilingualism Subtracts Up to 13 Years from Brain Age
Speaking another language could slow aging in the brain

chunks.text: Scientists have {{come up with}} a new way to measure how quickly the human brain grows older. At a large science [[conference]] in Europe, a research team from the Basque region of Spain {{pointed out}} that people who speak several languages often have younger brains than their [[chronological]] age would suggest. The team {{set out}} to test whether knowing more than one language can slow this kind of aging. Their early results suggest that it can.

chunks.text: The researchers used a form of [[artificial intelligence]] to {{work out}} each person's 'brain age' from patterns of brain [[connectivity]]. They looked at 144 people in the Basque region who spoke between one and four languages, such as Spanish, Basque, French, and English. As the number of languages grew, the brains appeared younger and younger. People who spoke two languages had brains that seemed about six years younger, while those who spoke four {{ended up}} with brains that looked around thirteen years younger.

chunks.text: The scientists say the number of languages is not the only thing that {{stands out}}. People who {{picked up}} a second language early in life, and who reached a high level of [[proficiency]], seemed to {{hold on to}} the benefit more strongly. Being truly [[fluent]] appeared to matter just as much as speaking many languages. Constantly switching between languages may give the brain a kind of daily workout that keeps it healthy.

chunks.text: These findings match a much larger project that {{looked into}} the health of 86,149 older people across 27 European countries. In that [[survey]], people who spoke several languages were about half as likely to show fast, unhealthy aging. Experts say the two studies {{back up}} a simple message: it is never too late to start. Adults who {{take up}} a new language may slow some of the mental [[decline]] that often comes with age.

tf.s: The team set out to test whether knowing more than one language can slow brain aging.
tf.why: Correct. The researchers set out to test whether speaking several languages slows this kind of aging.

tf.s: People who spoke four languages ended up with brains that looked older than their real age.
tf.why: They ended up with brains that looked about thirteen years younger, not older.

tf.s: The scientists came up with a way to make people speak more languages instantly.
tf.why: They came up with a way to measure brain age, not a way to make people speak languages instantly.

tf.s: Experts say the two studies back up the idea that it is never too late to learn a language.
tf.why: The story says the studies back up the message that it is never too late to start.

tf.s: A larger project looked into the health of 86,149 people across 27 European countries.
tf.why: The bigger survey looked into the health of 86,149 older people in 27 European countries.

tf.s: The study found that people who picked up a second language early got fewer benefits.
tf.why: People who picked up a second language early and became fluent held on to the benefit more strongly, so they got more, not fewer, benefits.
